opti-1: South Florida. A sea of grass, as far as you can see.
opti-2: But look closer. Under the grass, there's water.
opti-4: The water flows south, slowly, only inches deep.
opti-5: Spoonbills sweep the shallow water for food.
opti-6: Alligators wait in the warm water.
opti-7: Why can some animals thrive in the Everglades while others cannot survive there at all?
29-01-welcome: Our film starts in a sea of grass in South Florida. First, inspect a golden plant that grows there by the millions.
29-01-lesson: Today you're a wetland scientist. Follow one year in the Everglades, test which homes fit which bodies, then walk the Glades to the sea.
29-01-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
29-01-assign: Time to show what you learned. Sort the animals, then draw one that fits right in.
how-29-01-compare: Put the warm water under one tray and the sea ice under the other: drag them, or tap one, then a tray. Press Run the test. Then swap.
how-29-01-wall: First, make a prediction. Then brush the glowing step: drag across it (or tap it again and again) until the photo shows.
how-29-01-det: Pick three cards, one at a time. Tap a clue, then name what the animal needs. Predict how well it survives in the Everglades, and watch its home appear.
how-29-01-partc: Draw one animal that survives well in the Everglades, in its Everglades home. Show the water and plants around it. Then write two labels.
